TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND MEMBERS OF THE CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  MEREDITH ELGUIRA, PLANNING DIRECTOR

THRU:  ELAINE JENG P.E., CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  VIEW PRESERVATION COMPLAINT - 61 EASTFIELD DRIVE (JUGE)

DATE:  June 01, 2021

BACKGROUND:
On October 28, 2020, Mr. Juge (Complainant), the property owner of 61 Eastfield Drive, filed an
application with the Planning and Community Services Department requesting for review before the
Committee on Trees and Views. Mr. Juge included letters and pictures he has sent to Dr. Tamayo and
Mr. Sierra (Vegetation-owners) showing how his views have been affected by Vegetation-owners' trees
and hedges.

Complainant's records show that he purchased his property in 1982. On July 15, 2018, Complainant sent
a letter to Vegetation-owners attempting to discuss the restoration of his views. Communication
regarding reconciliation went on until May 26, 2020, when the Complainant asked for mediation. Both
parties continued to communicate regarding mediation until October 9, 2020, when Vegetation-owners
asked who will be responsible for the mediator's fee. Records show that the Complainant never
responded to the question, thus ending all communication between the two parties.

Complainant claims that he has met the requirements of the Municipal Code because the mediation
phase has exceeded the 60-day period.

RHMC Section 17.26.040 - View impairment dispute resolution process.

B. Mediation.

1. If the initial reconciliation does not yield a resolution of the complaint, and the complainant wishes
to further utilize the procedures under this chapter, then the complainant must request, in writing, that
the vegetation owner enter into mediation. The vegetation owner shall have sixty days from the date of
the request for mediation to accept or reject the request in writing. The vegetation owner's failure to
respond within sixty days will be deemed a formal refusal of mediation and the complainant may
proceed to an advisory hearing before the Committee on Trees and Views.

2. The participants will have sixty days from the date of the filling of acceptance of mediation to select

  3
 a mediator. If they cannot agree on a mediator within sixty days, they may jointly request that the City
select a mediator. Any mediator which is selected pursuant to this subsection shall be provided with a
link to a copy of this chapter.

Per RHMC, the complainant may proceed to an advisory hearing before the Committee on Trees and
Views if Vegetation-owners fail to respond within 60 days. Vegetation-owners responded to
Complainant's request for mediation, however, Complainant stopped communicating with Vegetation-
owners. Based on the action of the Complainant not responding to the question, the Mediation Phase
has not been completed.

In addition, Vegetation-owners are requesting postponement of the public hearing. Mr. Sierra is out of
the country and will not be able to attend the meeting. Lastly, Dr. Tamayo has also stated that Mr. Juge
never responded to her question and thus, the mediation has not occurred.

DISCUSSION:
Rolling Hills Municipal Code Section 17.26.010 states:
"Owners and residents should maintain trees on their property in a healthy condition for both safety
reasons and for preservation of outward views. Before planting trees, owners and residents should
consider view blockage. By this chapter, the City establishes a process by which persons may seek to
preserve and restore views which existed at any time since they purchased the property from
unreasonable obstruction by the growth of vegetation. By this chapter the City also establishes a list of
factors to be considered in determining appropriate actions to restore views while preserving the rights
of property owners by not unreasonably reducing privacy or shade or other benefits provided by
vegetation on a property. When a view obstruction dispute arises, the parties should act reasonably to
resolve the dispute through friendly communication, thoughtful negotiation, compromise and other
traditional means, such as discussions with the appropriate neighbors."

Based on the actions stated above and the goal of the RHMC to resolve disputes through friendly
communication, thoughtful negotiation and compromise, Staff is recommending that the two parties
should continue and complete the Mediation Phase with the caveat that there will be an end date to the
Mediation Phase. This will allow both parties to finally resolve their dispute or provide them with the
freedom to proceed to the Advisory Phase which will provide both parties with a clear path forward.
Staff will continue to support and facilitate the process, when needed.

FISCAL IMPACT:
None.

RECOMMENDATION:

Staff recommends that the Committee on Trees and Views advise the complainant, Mr. Juge, and
vegetation owners, Dr. Tamayo and Mr. Sierra, to mediate their dispute and continue the hearing for 60
days from June 1, 2021. Staff recommends that the Committee impose the following conditions:

  1. City staff will assist the parties, upon joint request, in selecting a mediator – either by suggesting
  potential mediators or selecting a mediator for them.
  2. Neither party may request a CTV hearing before they have had one full day of mediation.
  3. If, after the first day of mediation and before the 60 days has expired, one or both of the parties
  believe that further mediation will be fruitless, one or both parties may submit a request in writing
  and must, under penalty of perjury, state that they attempted mediation in good faith but that

  4
   efforts have been and will be fruitless.
  4. If only one party requests a hearing, but the other wishes to continue mediation, the party
  requesting hearing shall so notify the other party. The hearing will move forward on the pre-
  assigned date or at an earlier date if feasible; however, the non-requesting party may present
  evidence at the hearing to rebut the requesting party’s assertion that mediation was attempted in
  good faith, and such evidence may go towards determining whether a pre-existing view exists and
  whether it has been obstructed. S e e RHMC sec. 17.26.050(A) (evaluation factors are non-
  exclusive).

Dear Mr. Juge:

  I am a Deputy City Attorney for the City of Rolling Hills (the “City”), and I write in follow-
up to your May 26, 2021 conversation with Meredith Elguira, the City’s Planning and Community
Services Director, about the “Request for Review by Committee on Trees and Views” submitted
by you to the City on or about October 28, 2020 (the “View Impairment Complaint”) and its
compliance with Section 17.26.040 of the Rolling Hills Municipal Code (“RHMC”).

I.  The View Preservation Ordinance

  That Section states in pertinent part:

  A. Initial Reconciliation.

  1. A complainant whose preexisting view is impaired shall first
  seek to informally resolve the impairment with the vegetation owner. The
  initial notification to the vegetation owner must be in writing, include a
  link to this chapter and contain the following language: “Failure of the
  vegetation owner to respond to the written request for initial reconciliation
  within sixty days from the date on the notification shall be deemed formal
  refusal by the vegetation owner to participate in the initial reconciliation.”
  Additionally, any written notification to the vegetation owner must include
  any supporting evidence of the view obstruction, (as described by Section
  17.26.050) and any requested remediation action. Remediation action may

II.  The View Impairment Complaint

  58
 Joe Juge
May 28, 2021
Page 3

  According to your View Impairment Complaint, the following is the relevant sequence of
events:

    December 2016 – May 2020: You, on the one hand, and Dr. Tamayo and Mr. Sierra
  (together, the “Vegetation Owners”), on the other, exchange multiple
  correspondences in an attempt to informally resolve your differences.

    May 26, 2020: You request mediation.

    July 25, 2020: The Vegetation Owners agree to mediation.

    August 13, 2020: You suggest two potential mediators.

    October 9, 2020: The Vegetation Owners ask you how the mediator will be paid.

    October 25, 2020: You file the View Impairment Complaint with the City.

III.  Application

  Neither you nor the Vegetation Owners strictly complied with the initial reconciliation
requirements of RHMC sec. 17.26.040(A)(1). However, your many exchanges over the 3½ years
constitute substantial compliance, and the mutual agreement to mediate described below serves as
a waiver by both parties of any deficiency in the initial reconciliation process.

  You properly requested that the Vegetation Owners mediate your dispute, pursuant to
RHMC sec. 17.26.040(B)(1). The Vegetation Owners timely agreed to mediate within the 60 days
allowed under RHMC sec. 17.26.040(B)(1). Thereafter, you suggested two mediators, and the
Vegetation Owners asked a relevant question about how the mediator’s fee was to be paid. There
is nothing in the View Impairment Complaint that shows you answered the Vegetation Owners’
question or engaged in any further discussion about commencing mediation. Instead,
approximately two weeks after the Vegetation Owners asked their question, you filed the View
Impairment Complaint.

  Pursuant to RHMC sec. 17.26.040(B)(2), when you and the Vegetation Owners could not
agree on a mediator within 60 days from the date of acceptance of mediation (i.e., by September
23, 2020), you had the right to “jointly request that the City select a mediator.” You did not have
a right to skip mediation and proceed directly to a public hearing before the CTV.

  On this record, you have not complied with the requirement to mediate (or even attempt to
mediate) your dispute pursuant to RHMC sec. 17.26.040(B), and therefore, the CTV has no
jurisdiction to hear your View Impairment Complaint under RHMC sec. 17.26.040(C), unless and
